prediction_question: For a chosen NOAA water-level station, will the daily maximum observed water level exceed its published minor flood threshold tomorrow?
prediction_time: End of the local day before the target day. Features are observed water levels only. NOAA tide predictions and model guidance are model output and must be excluded so the task stays an observation-only forecast.
target_definition: Binary: the daily maximum observed water level for the target day exceeds the station's NOS minor flood threshold from the CO-OPS metadata API, compared at datum=STND. The physical nos_minor threshold is retained by decision; it is not replaced with a per-station quantile merely to balance the classes (see measurements.target_threshold_decision).
datum_requirement: MUST use datum=STND. The published nos_minor threshold is in the station datum and the metadata API does not declare a datum. Comparing MLLW-referenced heights to nos_minor silently yields zero positives at every station; see measurements.datum_trap_measured.

Same page: "NOS requests that attribution be given whenever NOS material is reproduced and re-disseminated. Pursuant to 17 U.S.C. 403 ... stating that such material is not subject to copyright protection." CONSTRAINT READ ON THE SAME PAGE, honoured in the release: "This information shall not be modified in content and then presented as official government material" - any derived dataset must be labelled as derived and must not be presented as official NOS data. Corroborating: nauticalcharts.noaa.gov/data/data-licensing.html records NOAA data released under a CC0-1.0 public-domain dedication (CC BY 4.0 for some products), and the NCEI ISO metadata for CO-OPS stations carries the same CC0 waiver. Attributes: attribution requested as a courtesy, not required.
split_strategy: Temporal: train 2006-2021, eval 2022-2023, holdout 2024-2025, with thresholds taken from metadata (not estimated) so nothing leaks. Measured positives: train 1,279, eval 234, holdout 256. Effective independent events are about half those counts because flood days cluster at ~2 stations each. See measurements.split_capacity_measured.

measurements.stations_with_flood_thresholds_measured: CORRECTED 2026-09-19: 132 of 302. The earlier 302 came from the inventory's floodlevels expand being present, not from a numeric nos_minor. 170 stations publish no numeric nos_minor (the endpoint returns either a bare number or an object whose nos_minor is null). Measured by one request: stations.json?type=waterlevels&expand=floodlevels.
measurements.measured_on: 2026-09-18 via CO-OPS metadata and data APIs

datum_trap_measured.observation: Comparing hourly_height at datum=MLLW against nos_minor yields 0 exceeding days at all 12 sampled stations across 4,380 station-days - a false 'no positive class' result caused entirely by a datum mismatch.
datum_trap_measured.decisive_check: Boston 8443970 over 2018-01-03..2018-01-05, the bomb-cyclone record tide: MLLW peak 15.022 ft at 2018-01-04 18:00 (below nos_minor 15.85, so 'no flood'); STND peak 18.547 ft at the same timestamp (above threshold, correct).
datum_trap_measured.conclusion: nos_minor is expressed in the station datum. Use datum=STND.
datum_trap_measured.also_tried: CO-OPS dpapi/prod/webapi/htb.json (High Tide Flooding daily product) returned count 0 with an empty floodLikelihood list for every station, date and range tried, including Boston 2018 and ranges 7/31/365/366. Not usable from this host.

exceedance_base_rates_measured.method: one hourly_height request per station-year at datum=STND, units=english; daily max from hourly rows compared to nos_minor; hourly rows streamed and discarded
exceedance_base_rates_measured.caveat: Four stations have an annual maximum within 0.2 ft below threshold (Portland, Key West, San Francisco, Seattle), so their zero rates are sensitive to a small residual offset. The pooled 1.37% estimate is the defensible figure.

external_validation_measured.result: VALIDATED. For station-year 2025 the STND reconstruction matches NOAA's authoritative minCount at 12 of 12 stations: 60 flood days total against NOAA's 60. The rejected MLLW reconstruction produced 0.
external_validation_measured.endpoint_note: htf/daily.json reports count = the number of DAYS RETURNED (365), not a flood count; its per-day rows are {day: 'MM/DD/YYYY', maxWL, maxTime, minFlag, modFlag, majFlag, percent_completeness}. htf/annual.json is the authoritative source for counts.

sampling_resolution_measured.question: Does hourly sampling miss brief exceedances?
sampling_resolution_measured.answer: Yes, occasionally. Hourly daily maxima are a slight undercount of the true flood-day rate.
sampling_resolution_measured.method: daily maximum from 6-minute water_level versus daily maximum from hourly_height, same station-month, datum=STND
sampling_resolution_measured.aggregate: 1 day missed out of 17 caught across the three station-months examined, so the hourly-derived rate undercounts by roughly 6% of positive days in the periods tested.
sampling_resolution_measured.consequence: Label construction should use 6-minute data where the budget allows; the hourly rate 1.37% is a lower bound. 6-minute data is limited to one month per request, which is worker work.

target_threshold_decision.decision: KEEP the physical NOS minor flood threshold. Do not replace it with a per-station quantile merely to balance the classes.
target_threshold_decision.reasoning: nos_minor is a real, externally defined threshold with physical meaning, and it is now validated against NOAA's own product. A quantile threshold would invent the event and would not correspond to flooding. The class imbalance is a property of the phenomenon to be documented and handled with appropriate metrics, not engineered away.
target_threshold_decision.handling: Report base rates, use precision/recall-style metrics alongside AUC, and treat the base rate as an explicit baseline.

split_capacity_measured.question: Do the evaluation splits contain enough positive events for reliable scoring?
split_capacity_measured.source: NOAA htf/annual minCount, up to 107 years per station
split_capacity_measured.answer: Yes on counts, but the positives are temporally clustered, so effective independent events are about half the row count.
caveats: The positive rate is not stationary: it rises with sea level across the series (1.83% in train against 2.92% in holdout), so a temporal split carries systematic base-rate shift.
2025 (60 days across the 12 stations) is far below 2024 (196), so year-to-year variation is large and any single year is a noisy estimate.
Positive days cluster at about 2 stations per flood day, so 256 holdout positives are roughly 126 independent events.

regression_test.live_check: python3 candidates/noaa-tide-flooding/datum_check.py re-fetches both datums for both recorded windows; verified 2026-09-18, all four peaks reproduced with delta 0.000
regression_test.purpose: The Boston bomb-cyclone event is the guard: any datum handling that denies flooding during Boston's record tide is wrong.

measurements.note: The class is rare at nos_minor (0-4.7% per station-day, 1.37% pooled from hourly data, a lower bound). Accuracy is meaningless at this base rate; use precision/recall-style metrics alongside AUC and an explicit base-rate baseline. The physical threshold is retained by decision.

station_list_frozen_measured.question: Which stations can carry the task?
station_list_frozen_measured.rule: numeric nos_minor AND >= 18 of the 20 target years present in htf/annual minCount
station_list_frozen_measured.evidence: NOAA's own HTF annual product reports per-year flood-day counts; coverage of the 20 target years is the record-length evidence. 1 request per station.

split_capacity_frozen_list_measured.question: Do the splits carry enough positives once the station list is frozen?
split_capacity_frozen_list_measured.method: sum of NOAA htf/annual minCount per year over the 122 frozen stations; station-days counted as 365 per station-year that has a count
split_capacity_frozen_list_measured.cross_check: the daily product reproduced the same positive counts exactly for both evaluation splits (1,828 eval, 2,850 holdout), measured 2026-09-19
split_capacity_frozen_list_measured.caveat: the positive rate is not stationary: 1.68% train, 2.05% eval, 3.20% holdout, so a temporal split carries base-rate shift.

clustering_frozen_list_measured.question: How many independent flood days do the evaluation splits carry?
clustering_frozen_list_measured.method: distinct calendar days carrying at least one flood across the frozen stations, from htf/daily.json per station-year (minFlag)
clustering_frozen_list_measured.train: NOT MEASURED - recorded as unmeasured rather than guessed

extraction_cost_measured.basis: per-request figures measured on the coordinator (candidates/noaa-tide-flooding/cost_probe.py -> cost_probe_result.json) multiplied by the counted request set - not an estimate

per_request.daily_max_product: does not exist - the API answers HTTP 400 for product=daily_max, so verified daily maxima must be derived from 6-minute or hourly observations

extraction_cost_measured.not_measured: wall clock with concurrent requests: the figures above are single-threaded sums of measured per-request times. Parallelism on the worker size chosen for the build is unmeasured.
extraction_cost_measured.conclusion: 6-minute labels for the whole frozen list are a worker-scale backfill (29,160 requests, 15.2 GiB, ~13 h single-threaded), not a coordinator job; hourly is 12x cheaper but was measured to undercount ~6% of positive days.

review: Ready for construction on 2026-09-19. Contracts: redistribution read from the publishing portal (public domain, attribution requested, derived-not-official constraint recorded); prediction timing stated with an observations-only feature list; target derivable from the observed water level at datum=STND with the label source excludable; split capacity measured over the frozen 122-station list, eval 1,828 positives over 332 independent flood days and holdout 2,850 over 427. Extraction cost measured rather than estimated. The base rate at the physical threshold is 1.7-3.2%, which is a property of the phenomenon, not a defect: report precision/recall-style metrics beside AUC and use the base rate as the baseline.

Then qualify with skills/dataset-qualification on the full artifact before quoting any number.
